slides.title: Transport, Cities, and Urban Solutions
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 7 English, Unit 4: Transport, Cities, and Urban Solutions. In this unit you will explore how cities grow, how people move through them, and how communities around the world are finding creative solutions to make urban life better for everyone. You will read about transport systems, green innovations, and the challenges that cities face in East Africa and beyond. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Read and understand a passage about city transport and discuss its ideas in English.
Use prepositions of time and place (in, on, at) correctly and confidently.
Form the passive voice in the past simple, present simple, and with modal verbs.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to read and understand a passage about city transport and discuss its ideas in English. You will also use prepositions of time and place (in, on, at) correctly and confidently. You will also form the passive voice in the past simple, present simple, and with modal verbs. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: melancholy, exuberant, elated, vulnerable, wary, famished. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: Moving Through Mogadishu: A City in Motion
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes Moving Through Mogadishu: A City in Motion and An Interview About City Transport. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: Prepositions of Time and Place
bullets: Prepositions are small but powerful words that show how the other words in a sentence relate to each other, and the three most important prepositions of...
slides.narration: The first language focus is Prepositions of Time and Place. Prepositions are small but powerful words that show how the other words in a sentence relate to each other, and the three most important prepositions of time and place — in, on and at — make your English sound natural and precise when chosen correctly. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Vocabulary Expert Interview. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use AI English for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
